subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which two organs make up the central nervous system (CNS)?
options: The brain and the spinal cord
The spinal cord and the sensory organs
questions.explain: The CNS consists of the brain and spinal cord, which coordinate the body's responses.

questions.q: Which type of neurone carries impulses from receptors to the central nervous system?
questions.explain: Sensory neurones carry electrical impulses from receptors to the CNS.

questions.q: Which type of neurone carries impulses from the central nervous system to effectors?
questions.explain: Motor neurones carry impulses from the CNS to effectors such as muscles and glands.

questions.q: What is the name of the small gap between two neurones where impulses are passed on?
questions.explain: A synapse is the tiny gap between neurones, across which a chemical (neurotransmitter) carries the signal.

questions.q: Which sequence correctly shows the pathway of a nervous response?
options: Stimulus → receptor → sensory neurone → CNS → motor neurone → effector → response
Stimulus → effector → CNS → motor neurone → receptor → response
Receptor → stimulus → motor neurone → CNS → sensory neurone → response
Stimulus → motor neurone → receptor → CNS → sensory neurone → effector
questions.explain: A stimulus is detected by a receptor, passed via a sensory neurone to the CNS, then via a motor neurone to an effector producing a response.

questions.q: Effectors that carry out a response to a nervous impulse are:
questions.explain: Effectors are muscles (which contract) or glands (which secrete), producing the response.

questions.q: A reflex action is best described as a response that is:
questions.explain: Reflex actions are rapid, automatic responses that do not require conscious thought.

questions.q: In a reflex arc, which neurone connects the sensory neurone to the motor neurone within the spinal cord?
questions.explain: The relay neurone links the sensory and motor neurones inside the CNS, allowing a fast reflex response.

questions.q: A person touches a sharp pin and instantly pulls their hand away before feeling pain. Why does the hand move before the pain is felt?
options: The reflex arc bypasses conscious processing in the brain, so the response happens first
Hormones act faster than nerves in this situation
The pain receptors are switched off during a reflex
The motor neurone sends the impulse directly to the brain
questions.explain: The reflex arc produces movement via the spinal cord before impulses reach the brain, so the hand withdraws before pain is consciously felt.

questions.q: Why are reflex actions important for survival?
options: They protect the body from harm by producing very fast responses
They allow the body to learn new skills
They control the release of hormones into the blood
They slow down responses to allow careful decisions
questions.explain: Reflexes are protective because their speed and automatic nature reduce damage from harmful stimuli.

questions.q: How are hormones transported around the body?
questions.explain: Hormones are chemical messengers released by glands and carried in the bloodstream to target organs.

questions.q: Which organ produces the hormone insulin?
questions.explain: Insulin is secreted by the pancreas and lowers blood glucose concentration.

questions.q: Compared with nervous responses, hormonal (chemical) responses are generally:
options: Slower to act but longer lasting
Faster to act and shorter lasting
questions.explain: Hormones travel in the blood, so their effects are slower to begin but usually last longer than rapid nervous responses.

questions.q: The hormone adrenaline is produced by the:
questions.explain: Adrenaline is released by the adrenal glands, preparing the body for action ('fight or flight').

questions.q: A student feels frightened before an exam and notices their heart is beating faster. Which hormone is most likely responsible?
questions.explain: Adrenaline increases heart rate and prepares the body for action in response to fear or stress.

questions.q: Homeostasis is best defined as:
options: The maintenance of a constant internal environment in the body
The rapid movement of nerve impulses
The release of hormones from glands
The detection of stimuli by receptors
questions.explain: Homeostasis keeps internal conditions, such as temperature and blood glucose, steady despite external changes.

questions.q: When blood glucose concentration rises too high after a meal, the pancreas releases insulin. What effect does insulin have?
options: It lowers blood glucose by causing the liver to store glucose
It raises blood glucose by releasing stored glucose
It increases the breakdown of proteins
questions.explain: Insulin causes cells and the liver to take up and store glucose, returning blood glucose to normal.

questions.q: A runner becomes very hot during a race. Which of the following responses helps cool the body down?
options: Sweating and widening of blood vessels near the skin (vasodilation)
Shivering and narrowing of blood vessels
Reduced blood flow to the skin
Contraction of hair erector muscles to trap air
questions.explain: Sweating removes heat through evaporation and vasodilation increases heat loss from the skin, cooling the body.

questions.q: Homeostatic control often works by negative feedback. This means that:
options: A change from the normal level triggers a response that reverses the change
A change is amplified to move further from normal
The body ignores small changes in conditions
Hormones and nerves stop working together
questions.explain: In negative feedback, a deviation from the set level triggers a corrective response that returns the condition to normal.

questions.q: A person with diabetes cannot make enough insulin. What is a likely consequence for their blood glucose?
options: Blood glucose can rise to dangerously high levels
Blood glucose is always too low
Blood glucose is stored too quickly by the liver
questions.explain: Without enough insulin, glucose is not stored effectively, so blood glucose can rise dangerously high.
